Spec-compliance review of US-10-01 (diff main...94a466b): NOT COMPLIANT. One blocking finding: the Ollama check honours the system's HTTP proxy, so criterion #4 and `MOD-10-NFR-02` fail on any computer where a proxy is set.

Spec: /home/sulo/workspace/private/calendar-buddy/docs/specs/modules/10-events-from-a-description/stories/US-10-01-ollama-settings.md

**Tests.** I ran them on 94a466b. All of TC-10-01, 02, 03, 06 and 07 passed, plus `ollama::tests`, `shortcuts::tests`, `settings::tests` and `description::tests::ollama_is_asked_only_at_its_address_and_google_nothing`: 9 passed in the app crate, 27 in core. Between my calls the working tree moved from detached 94a466b to main (05db4f0). I changed nothing; both test runs happened while it was still at 94a466b.

## Criteria table

| # | Criterion / requirement | Verdict | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | Settings section, defaults, kept after a restart | MET | `ollama.rs:30-38`, `settings.rs` parse/save, `description.rs:127-162`. Test `tc_10_01_…` passes. |
| 2 | Unticked: box, `q` and its list entry gone; back when ticked | MET | `main.rs:2587` (box only when on), `shortcuts.rs` `command`/`listed(descriptions)`. Tests `tc_10_02_…` and `with_events_from_a_description_off_q_…` pass. |
| 3 | Warning for an address off this computer, none for local ones | MET | `ollama.rs:53-63`, `description.rs:155-157`. Test `tc_10_03_…` passes. |
| 4 | Default address: no request to anything but Google and this computer | NOT MET | See B1: with a proxy set in the environment, the default-address check goes to the proxy host. |
| 5 | README section | external (MANUAL TC-10-05) | Checked by reading `README.md` (+110-141): ollama.com links, `ollama pull gemma4:e4b`, and "works without Ollama and the model" are there. Following it end to end is the owner's manual step. |
| 6 | Ollama not running: box greyed out, reason, link to settings | MET | `description.rs:87-124`, `ollama.rs:80-86`. `tc_10_06_…` steps 1-2 pass, including the link opening the settings scrolled to the section. |
| 7 | Model missing: same, naming the model | MET | `tc_10_06_…` step 3 passes. |
| 8 | Ollama starts later: available without a restart | MET | `main.rs:1964-1990` (going to the box asks Ollama again). `tc_10_07_…` steps 1-3 pass. |
| Covers | F19, F20, F21, F26, U04, U05 | delivered | As in rows #1-#3 and #5-#8. |
| Covers | MOD-10-NFR-02 | NOT delivered | "The only network traffic the function adds goes to the Ollama address set" fails under B1 (and N1). |

**Edge cases**
- Ollama stops while the box is open: implemented (Enter asks Ollama again) and tested by TC-10-07 step 2.
- Invalid URL: kept-previous is unit-tested (`an_address_that_is_not_one_is_refused_and_the_previous_one_kept`). That "the settings say so" on screen is not tested (N3).

**Are the BLOCKED markings legitimate?**
- **TC-10-07 step 4:** legitimate. It needs a description sent and the "New event" window, which is US-10-02's out-of-scope item (DEC-215). Criterion #8 is fully proven by steps 1-3, so I count #8 as met, not blocked.
- **TC-10-04 as written:** legitimately blocked, since it sends "Kawa jutro o 10".
- **Criterion #4 itself:** this one does not rest on US-10-02. Its claim already applies to the traffic this story adds (the version and model-list checks), and that traffic is wrong under B1. So #4 is a genuine NOT MET, not an external block. The partial evidence given doesn't prove the claim either: the "google nothing" test never involves Google (N2).

## Findings

**B1 [security] `crates/core/src/ollama.rs:92-95`**
- **Defect:** `ollama::check` builds its ureq agent from `Config::default()`. In ureq 3.5.0 that reads `ALL_PROXY`/`HTTPS_PROXY`/`HTTP_PROXY` (`config.rs:1073`) and does not exempt loopback addresses. `NO_PROXY` is honoured only if the user lists localhost in it.
- **Failing scenario:** with `HTTP_PROXY` set on the user's computer, the request to `http://localhost:11434` goes to the proxy host. That breaks #4 and `MOD-10-NFR-02`, and Ollama is wrongly reported as not running (#6). US-10-02 will send descriptions through the same pattern.
- **Reproduced:** `env -u NO_PROXY HTTP_PROXY=http://192.0.2.1:3128 cargo test -p calendar-core ollama::tests::ollama_is_asked` fails at `ollama.rs:364` (left: NotRunning, right: Available). The request went to 192.0.2.1, off this computer.
- **Fix:** `.proxy(None)` on the Ollama agent's config builder, plus a test that sets a proxy variable and still reaches the fake Ollama.

**Non-blocking**
- **N1 `crates/core/src/ollama.rs:92-95`:** ureq follows up to 10 redirects by default. Something answering at the local address with a redirect sends the check (and later the description) to another host, which contradicts "Nothing else leaves the app" (REQUIREMENTS, Integrations). Fix: `.max_redirects(0)`.
- **N2 `crates/app/src/description.rs:577-604`:** the test `ollama_is_asked_only_at_its_address_and_google_nothing` has no fake Google and asserts nothing about Google; it only checks the fake Ollama's own record. It also never records requests to any other host, so it could not catch B1. Fix: rename it, or add a check that no other host was asked (e.g. a proxy variable pointing at a recorder, after B1's fix).
- **N3 `crates/app/src/description.rs:152-154`:** the second edge case's "the settings say so" (the `NOT_AN_OLLAMA_ADDRESS` label) has no UI-level test; only the `Form` logic is unit-tested. Fix: one harness test entering an invalid address and checking the label is shown and `settings.ollama.address` is unchanged.
- **N4 `crates/app/src/description.rs:217-220`:** the test harness repeats the start-up ask itself instead of exercising `CalendarApp::new` (`main.rs:461-464`), so "checked at start" in the real constructor is untested.
- **N5 `crates/core/src/ollama.rs:91`:** the module's Technical notes ask for the Ollama client "behind an interface like the calendar provider (NFR-14)". `check` is a free function hard-wired to ureq. DEC-216 says it follows the notes but does not. It can wait for US-10-02's client, but DEC-216's wording is inaccurate.
- **N6 `scripts/cargo_report.py` (whole file, commit 96a293e):** delivery-loop tooling (cargo output to a Playwright JSON report) that no requirement of this story asks for. Under the surgical-diff rule it belongs in its own chore change.
- **N7 `crates/app/src/main.rs:1981`:** Enter in the box asks Ollama again, an interim behaviour no criterion asks for (recorded in DEC-215). US-10-02 must replace it rather than build on it.
- **N8 `docs/specs/constitution.md:57`:** still says "The only network traffic is HTTPS to Google's APIs". Ollama uses plain HTTP under the NFR-06 exception (DEC-207), which the constitution does not reflect. This is drift outside the diff; worth a note for the tech lead.
- **N9:** the story spec and `docs/specs/BACKLOG.md` still say `in-progress`. The definition of done asks for the status to be updated, presumably later in the loop.

Constitution: apart from B1 against the NFR-06 / "only network traffic" rules, nothing in the diff breaks the stack or architecture rules. Checks run off the UI thread (`description.rs:26-48`) and nothing is logged.
